info.title: About this workspace
info.spin_analysis: Plots the pulsar's spin frequency (F0) and its derivative (F1) over time, comparing the observed values from loaded DAT data against the model computed from the PAR file, with and without glitches. Use the graph and line toggles above to choose which panels (F0, F1, Phase, ΔF0, ΔF1) and which curves (observed, model, model without glitches) are visible. Glitch epochs are marked on the timeline.
info.glitches_toas: Shows, for each loaded project with glitches, a timeline of the TOA (Time of Arrival) coverage around every glitch epoch: how many TOAs fall before and after the glitch within the selected search window, the time to the nearest TOA, and the median timing uncertainty. Click a glitch marker on the plot to list the individual nearby TOAs. Adjust the search window (± days) above to widen or narrow what counts as "nearby".
info.residuals: Plots the frequency residuals (observed − model) for each loaded project that has both a PAR model and DAT observations, showing how well the fitted spin/glitch model matches the measured data over time. The summary panel below reports the RMS, reduced χ², and number of points per project.
info.datasets: Lists every loaded project (each group of PAR/DAT/TIM files) with its identified pulsar name, which file types are loaded, the number of observations and TOAs, the number of glitch components in the model, and the MJD span covered by its data. Use the checkboxes in the left panel to show or hide each project across all tabs.

information.html:
About PulsarLab

This page describes exactly what each main view displays and what data it needs.

Spin Analysis

Purpose: inspect the rotational evolution predicted by the PAR timing model and compare it with DAT observations when available.

  • F0: rotational frequency in Hz. With DAT loaded, observed values are drawn together with the model. The “no glitches” curve is the same timing model evaluated without glitch terms.
  • F1: first derivative of rotational frequency, displayed in 10^-15 Hz/s. DAT F1 values are shown when the file contains them.
  • Phase: integrated rotational phase of the model in cycles, shifted so the displayed model starts at zero phase.
  • ΔF0 and ΔF1: the isolated glitch contribution, calculated as the model including glitches minus the same model without glitches.
  • Glitch rails: dotted vertical lines and G labels mark physical glitch epochs (GLEP). Components sharing the same GLEP are grouped as one event.

F0 and F1 are enabled by default. The graph and line controls can show or hide diagnostic panels, observed data, the model, the no-glitch baseline, and glitch markers. The MJD range controls change the visible time interval.

Glitches & TOAs

Purpose: inspect the temporal relationship between glitches from the PAR model and pulse Times of Arrival (TOAs) from a TIM file.

  • Upper graph: one horizontal row per project. TIM TOAs appear as vertical marks; glitches appear as labelled markers. The shaded area around each glitch is the selected ±TOA search window.
  • Lower graph: positive finite TOA uncertainties in microseconds, displayed on a logarithmic y-axis. Dotted vertical lines indicate glitch epochs.
  • Text summary: for every glitch it reports GLEP MJD, number of TOAs inside the selected window, counts before/after the glitch, signed time to the nearest TOA in days, median TOA uncertainty, and a contextual coverage indicator.
  • Coverage: GOOD means at least 10 nearby TOAs and at least 25% of all nearby TOAs on each side of the glitch; LIMITED means at least 5 nearby TOAs but the GOOD condition is not met; POOR means fewer than 5 nearby TOAs. This is a sampling-coverage heuristic, not a measurement of timing precision.
  • Glitch click: selecting a glitch marker shows its GLPH/GLF0/GLF1/GLF2/GLF0D/GLTD components and up to the 25 nearest TOAs inside the current search window.

A PAR file is needed to define glitches. A TIM file is needed to display TOAs and uncertainty/coverage information.

Residuals

Purpose: compare processed DAT frequencies with the PAR model at the same MJD values.

  • F0 residual: observed F0 − model F0, in Hz.
  • F1 residual: observed F1 − model F1, in Hz/s, when DAT contains F1.
  • Text summary: reports F0 RMS, reduced χ² when valid positive uncertainties are available, and the number of finite residuals.

This view requires PAR + DAT. These are processed-frequency residuals; they are not full barycentric TOA timing residuals.

Projects

Purpose: provide a compact overview of every visible PulsarLab project and its loaded components.

  • If DAT exists, the graph shows observed F0 versus MJD. If there is no DAT but a PAR model is computable, it shows model F0 instead.
  • TIM TOAs are shown as a compact rug of vertical marks along the lower edge of the graph because TOAs do not have an F0 ordinate.
  • The text summary lists pulsar identification, loaded file types, number of DAT observations, number of TOAs, number of glitch components, and the available MJD span.
  • The left navigator controls which projects are visible. Clicking a project makes it active; the +PAR, +DAT and +TIM controls attach a missing component to the active project when possible, otherwise they create a new project.
